subject: Post-demo: mapping of prompt-derived PII, storage paths, and audit window
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acercahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: mapping of prompt-derived PII, storage paths, and audit window

Hi Tom / Priya / security team —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Per our conversation, I wanted to put a concise mapping of what Redwood stores (if anything) for a typical prompt -> output interaction and the associated audit/retention options so your security team can review quickly. See the short answers first, then the detailed rows.

Short summary (TL;DR):
- By default in Redwood Hosted API: request prompts and model outputs are stored transiently for up to 30 days for telemetry and quality monitoring by default; PII fields can be redacted or excluded via customer config.
- For Enterprise Dedicated/Private: customers can opt out of storage entirely (ephemeral-only), or configure an export-only mode where derivatives are forwarded to your storage (S3/EU-region) and Redwood retains only non-identifying telemetry.
- Auditing: access logs (who requested what) are retained for 365 days by default for Dedicated contracts; SOC 2 evidence exports available on request.

Concrete mapping (attached PDF has the tabular export):
- Raw prompt payload: stored if "persist_prompts" enabled; otherwise ephemeral. Option to redact specific sensitive fields using pattern rules or named field masking prior to storage.
- Model-generated output: stored in "session cache" ephemeral by default; persisted only when "persist_outputs" is enabled. Persisted outputs can be stored in customer-owned buckets for Private deployments.
- Derivative artifacts (embeddings, reranker scores, trace logs): configurable; embeddings are typically considered derived PII if they can be linked back to a person — we treat them per your policy.
- KV cache / session context (in memory): never written to disk in ephemeral mode; persisted to encrypted volumes only in Dedicated/Private when requested.

Action items / next steps I propose:
1) Marcus to share a short export (redwood-prompt-data-map.pdf) showing exact object paths and field names we saw during demo. (attached)
2) Tom/Priya/security to mark which fields are considered PII-sensitive for your internal policy; we will provide masking rules and a config snippet.
3) Confirm desired retention windows per artifact (prompts, outputs, embeddings, access logs). We can support 0d (ephemeral), 30d, 90d, 365d, or custom ranges for Dedicated.

If useful, we can schedule a 30-minute tech-run with Marcus (runtime) and our privacy engineer to walk the data flow and show the S3 export flow and audit log packaging.

Thanks — and attaching the one-page mapping + SOC2 logs summary we mentioned.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Post-demo: mapping of prompt-derived PII, storage paths, and audit window

Irene — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the artifacts. A few clarifying questions from our InfoSec and product teams:  

1) When you say "transiently for up to 30 days", is that retention configurable per customer? We need to be able to set an account-level policy to 0 days (no persistence).

2) For persisted outputs that are stored in customer buckets, can you confirm the default encryption-at-rest and whether objects are tagged with any Redwood identifiers that could leak metadata outside our tenancy? We prefer zero vendor tags on customer-owned buckets.

3) Embeddings: our data classification policy treats vectorized representations of PII as sensitive. If we choose to keep embeddings (for search), does Redwood offer automated hashing or reversible tokenization so we can assert non-re-identifiability?

4) Audit exports: you mentioned SOC2 evidence exports — can that include raw access logs with request/response object references (not full responses) and a signed manifest? Our auditors typically want request IDs and hashes, not the payloads.

Also looping in security@acercahealth.com — please flag anything I missed. We prefer a short tech run to validate configuration.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: mapping of prompt-derived PII, storage paths, and audit window

Tom — thanks for the great questions. Quick answers inline and a sample config snippet below. Happy to demo livesetup.

1) Retention per account: yes. Hosted accounts can set a tenant policy to 0d (ephemeral) or any of the supported windows. For Dedicated/Private we provide a flag: "persist_mode: off|ephemeral|customer_bucket|redwood_persist". Off = no writes; ephemeral = in-memory cache only; customer_bucket = objects are written to your S3 with no Redwood metadata tags by default; redwood_persist = Redwood-managed encrypted blobstore.

2) Encryption & tagging: customer_bucket writes use server-side encryption with the KMS key you supply (SSE-KMS). We do not apply Redwood vendor tags to objects written to customer buckets unless you opt in for debugging. By default we set only a minimal manifest entry in the export log (request_id, object_key, sha256) — no vendor-identifying metadata in the object itself.

3) Embeddings: we support two modes: (a) deterministic one-way hashing of embeddings (not reversible) at write-time; (b) reversible tokenization restricted by HSM-wrapped keys for private deployments on Dedicated/Private (requires contract addendum). For your use-case I recommend deterministic hashing + per-embedding salt (rotated quarterly). This satisfies non-re-identifiability for most auditors; we can provide the hashing proof in the SOC2 export.

4) Audit exports: yes — we can produce a signed manifest (SHA256) with request_id, timestamp, object_key (if persisted), user_id, and operation type. Payloads are excluded. We can also produce an HMAC-signed index for auditors.

Sample config (snip):

persist_mode: customer_bucket
customer_bucket: s3://acerca-prod-llm-outputs
encryption: SSE-KMS
kms_key_arn: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789:key/abcd-ef01
redact_fields: ["patient_ssn","patient_name","contact_phone"]
embedding_mode: hash_salted
retention_windows: {prompts: 0d, outputs: 90d, embeddings: 365d, access_logs: 365d}

I'll set up a 30-min tech-run next week; how does Thu 12/23 11am PT look for you? If that works I'll include our privacy engineer and the runtime lead.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | (650) 555-0199
